items.headline: SpaceX's AI segment reaches $7.5B of $14.6B Q3 revenue; Q4 capex guided to $35-40B
items.why: AI compute is now over half the revenue of a company known for rockets, and a $35-40B quarterly spend signals the infrastructure build-out is still accelerating, not plateauing.

sources.title: SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations

items.headline: Supermicro raises quarterly guidance on AI server demand; shares close up about 9.6%
items.why: A hardware vendor lifting guidance is direct evidence that AI server orders are still outrunning supply, which supports the chip and data-centre supply chain.

sources.title: Market recap: SpaceX, Meta, Tesla, Supermicro

items.headline: Meta guides 2026 capex to $135-145B; Tesla cuts its 2026 capex plan to about $20B
items.why: Hyperscale AI spending keeps climbing at Meta while Tesla pulls back, so the spending cycle is diverging by company rather than rising uniformly.

items.headline: Markets price an 83% chance the Fed holds on Oct. 27-28 and about 94% odds of a hike by Dec. 9
items.why: With September CPI at 3.7% year on year and PPI at 6.3%, the policy path is priced as tightening, which keeps pressure on long-duration assets and gold.

items.headline: New attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz; Iran's foreign minister says near-term peace prospects are limited
items.why: Direct Hormuz flows are about a third below prewar levels, so the conflict is feeding energy prices and inflation, which in turn drives the rate path.

items.headline: September housing starts fall 5.2% to 1.221M, well below the 1.305M expected
items.why: Rate-sensitive housing is weakening under higher yields, the kind of labour and activity softness traders need to see before tightening expectations ease.
